- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 10-day moving average), reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward correction for first 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
